message.reasoning_content:
The t10/t11 probes failed due to default dtype (torch.tensor defaults to float32; .to(dev) preserves dtype). Fix by specifying dtype=torch.float16.

t9 result: c1 probe found 0 violations, max ratio 0.225. That's a benign result — near-cancelling inputs with b up to ±65504 but a = -b*d/c quantization makes a large relative... hmm, but note the exact real component was ~7e-7, tolerance 1e-7... error 4e-14, fine. Actually the test was weak: a ≈ -b*d/c quantized to FP16 introduces error ~ b*d/c relative ulp, making the "near-cancellation" not tight. Actually with a=8.2 and b=34240, cancellation to ~1e-6 relative 1e-7 — but the errors were small. Interesting: since a is small and b*ratio is large... wait, b*ratio = 34240*(0.49/2048)=8.2. Both operands ~8.2, error ~1e-15 * scale ~ 2048 → real err ~ 4e-13... observed 4e-14. Fine — FP32 has plenty of precision here because a and b*ratio are only ~8, not 65504. The claim's scenario requires a itself to be large, i.e., c small relative to d. To make b*ratio ~ 65504 need |ratio|~1, but then minor≈major, d≈c. E.g. c=1, d=0.9995, b=65504, a=-b*d/c≈-65471. Then real numerator cancellation with operands ~65471, error ~65471*6e-8*... divided by scale ~2 → ~2e-3 absolute error. That's the true c1 scenario! t9's design was flawed (c=2048 dominates d, making a small).

So relaunch c1 with c≈d design. Fix c2 and c3 with dtype=torch.float16.

Finalize t9: it rebutted the specific scenario tested but the claim scenario not properly exercised — mark inconclusive? The claim says "e.g. a ≈ -b*d/c" with large components. My t9 test had large b but small a. I'll mark t9 as inconclusive (probe didn't realize the worst-case conditioning) and relaunch a proper c1 probe.

Batch: finalize t9 (inconclusive), relaunch c1, c2, c3 fixed probes.
